findings.reason: The protected split-and-hash implementation is clear and Accepted but repeats slicing, reversal, and palindrome scans, taking O(nk^2 + P) rather than the Reference's required linear work in total characters. The sole inert candidate precomputes exact palindromic boundaries with delimiter-expanded Manacher and queries a reverse trie in O(S + P), while also replacing exact local index names with conventional i and j.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 336 and its Python palindromePairs surface. The Reference preserves distinct lowercase words including the empty string, ordered distinct-index pairs, all three explained source examples, all three constraints, and the stated total-character runtime requirement.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064449306 and structurally aligns with the protected app-local split implementation apart from the required class wrapper and legacy List annotations. The materially different candidate remains app-local and inert; it has no remote submission evidence and must not replace either protected source without exact-byte Accepted verification.

The rebuilt legal tiers contain 400, 3,200, and 19,200 total characters and jointly grow word count and length without producing output pairs. The candidate passes all nine executions at -0.00 relative growth and 6.94x; correct all-pairs concatenation passes all three benchmark outputs but fails only scaling at +0.24. Exhaustive boundary checks over 255 binary strings and differential checks over 1,200 distinct-word sets independently validate the candidate's linear preprocessing and pair logic.

The candidate-targeted Approach now exactly derives delimiter-expanded Manacher boundary flags, reverse-trie insertion annotations, terminal and longer-partner query cases, empty-string handling, completeness, and O(S + P) time and space with S defined as total input characters.

The hash-bound public Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including all three source examples and explanations in order, all three constraints, distinct-word and empty-string semantics, and the source's total-character runtime requirement.
